parsed_tool.name: Split Paired and Unpaired
parsed_tool.description: into separate paired and unpaired collections

help.content:
========
Synopsis
========

Splits a collection into separate paired and unpaired output collections.

===========
Description
===========

This tool separates a collection that may contain a mix of paired-end and single-end datasets into two output collections:

- **Paired output** (``list:paired``) — elements that have both forward and reverse components.
- **Unpaired output** (``list``) — single (unpaired) elements.

The tool accepts ``list``, ``list:paired``, or ``list:paired_or_unpaired`` input collections. If the input is a plain ``list`` (all unpaired), all elements go to the unpaired output and the paired output is empty. If the input is ``list:paired`` (all paired), all elements go to the paired output and the unpaired output is empty.

========
Examples
========

**Split a mixed collection**

Given a ``list:paired_or_unpaired`` collection::

 Input:

   sample1  →  forward + reverse  (paired)
   sample2  →  single dataset     (unpaired)
   sample3  →  single dataset     (unpaired)

The tool produces::

 Paired output (list:paired):

   sample1  →  forward + reverse

 Unpaired output (list):

   sample2  →  Dataset 1
   sample3  →  Dataset 2

-------

.. image:: ${static_path}/images/tools/collection_ops/split_paired_unpaired.svg
  :alt: Split paired and unpaired elements
  :width: 620

-------

.. class:: infomark

This tool will create new history datasets copied from your input collections but your quota usage will not increase.
